correctness.rationale: Full 16-vertex universe is enumerated by an explicit nonzero-distinct 16-signature predicate; all 65536 code masks are considered, proving strict minimum 7 and 960 minima. Exact two-bit xor swaps yield 4320 edges, all degrees 9, twelve local triangles. The 384 Hamming-isometry actions exhaust three orbits 384+384+192; BFS from each representative yields the same complete distance shells and radius/diameter 7. A second independently encoded checker considers all six- and seven-element subsets, constructs edges using common six-subsets and BFS from all 960 states, confirming every number. Both separately detect 192 weak distinct-only six-codes, excluding a normalization error. Two standalone programs and their output files were executed from actual package paths; the argument is strictly finite.

value.rationale: An optimal identifying code is a minimum-cost fault-location sensor deployment; exchanging just one sensor is a natural robustness question and may fail in other optimal-code families. This theorem shows every pair of optimum four-cube deployments can be transformed while keeping all vertices distinguishable and covered, with precisely seven swaps needed in the worst case, nine local safe options from any state, and a common exact profile across three non-equivalent Hamming-symmetry types. This precise optimum-configuration geometry is not recoverable from the known scalar bound seven or the presence of one identifying code, making it a motivated, complete classification rather than an arbitrary isolated count.
